validated_results.title: Trace Element Concentrations of Arsenic and Selenium in Toenails and Risk of Prostate Cancer among Pesticide Applicators.
validated_results.reason: This nested case-control study evaluates the association between toenail selenium concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk among pesticide applicators.

extraction.population: Agricultural Health Study pesticide applicators in Iowa

sample_size.excerpt: Table S1: Comparison from the nested case-control study of 232 responders and 228 non-responders based on elements of the Agricultural Health Study Enrollment Questionnaire.

cases.excerpt: Trace elements among 59 prostate cancer cases and 173 healthy male controls selected within the Iowa portion of the Agricultural Health Study cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: An increased risk was seen for the highest levels of arsenic (OR = 3.4 confidence interval (CI) of 1.3–8.6 and OR = 2.2, 95% CI of 0.9–5.6) and the highest level of selenium (2.0, 95% CI of 1.0–4.0).

confidence_interval.excerpt: An increased risk was seen for the highest levels of arsenic (OR = 3.4 confidence interval (CI) of 1.3–8.6 and OR = 2.2, 95% CI of 0.9–5.6) and the highest level of selenium (2.0, 95% CI of 1.0–4.0).

design.excerpt: We conducted a nested case-control study of prostate cancer within Iowa participants of the AHS cohort

timing.excerpt: We conducted a nested case-control study of prostate cancer within Iowa participants of the AHS cohort

continent.excerpt: Prostate cancer is a common cancer among males in the US

location.excerpt: men residing in Iowa within the Agricultural Health Study cohort

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Neutron Activation Analysis (NAA), a sensitive analytical technique, was used to measure the long-lived indicators of trace elements in the toenails.

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
